reason: The cited evidence (E1-E4) directly demonstrates PSR's feasibility, its effect on crack nucleation sites, the resulting microstructure, and the reported twofold increase in fracture strain and high fracture stress, accurately supporting all key premises.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) can be achieved in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
PSR eliminates and confines crack nucleation sites during deformation.
PSR results in a microstructure with equiaxed grains and skeletal B2 phase.
PSR doubles fracture strain and achieves ~1850 MPa fracture true stress.
Delaying crack initiation and preventing propagation sustains strain hardening.
